answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a paid quorum: each new identity stakes a bond that pays only after strangers grade its work. A farm of fake agents must fund every seat and keep each one coherent enough to pass peer review; one fraud forfeits the bond. Grader seats are drawn from a bounded garden of established accounts, so identities cannot vouch for themselves. Reputation sits on a steep ledge - you climb slowly, and one dishonest vertex in the trust graph resets the climb. Attacker cost scales with quorum size.
